statement: You are given a string s. A subsequence is formed by deleting zero or more characters of s without changing the order of the rest.

Count the non-empty subsequences of s that are palindromes. Subsequences are counted by the positions they use, so two subsequences made from different positions count separately even when they spell the same string.

Return that count. A 2D table dp[i][j], the count for s[i … j], gives it in O(n²) time: dp[i][j] = dp[i + 1][j] + dp[i][j − 1] + 1 when s[i] equals s[j], and dp[i + 1][j] + dp[i][j − 1] − dp[i + 1][j − 1] otherwise.

examples.explanation: There are the four single letters, "cc", "bb", "bcb" twice (once with each c) and "bccb": 4 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 9.
Every non-empty choice of positions spells only a's and is a palindrome, so all 2³ − 1 = 7 of them count.
